newsitem.title: POLAND: Polish rail deal opens way for Adtranz investment.
newsitem.headline: Polish rail deal opens way for Adtranz investment.

text.p: Polish State Railways (PKP) on Thursday clinched an initial deal with Pafawag SA to buy 50 locomotives. This could trigger Pafawag's sale to Adtranz, a joint venture between ABB and Daimler-Benz.
PKP said that under the initial deal, to be followed by more talks before a final agreement is signed, the first locomotives will be delivered in 1997. @
Adtranz has said it will buy Pafawag if it wins the PKP contract.
In a tentative agreement with the government in September, Adtranz said it would pay $3.7 million for a 75 percent stake in Pafawag and invest $28.1 million over the next six years.
The agreement will take effect when Pafawag and PKP agree on a locomotive delivery programme. @
Adtranz would then increase Pafawag's capital by $6 million and start production of high-speed electric locomotives. Pafawag's employment would be maintained at the current level of 1,620 people.
An Adtranz official said on Thursday the company would issue a statement later in the day.
